title: Attention kernels exploration notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick running notes + experiment log for attention-kernel profiling work. Goal is to collect reproducible microbenchmarks across FlashAttention, paged attention, and our fused-attention kernels to understand latency tail, memory behavior, and where batching/kv-cache pressure causes regressions. This is a working doc — messy, checkpoints + TODOs included.

Background / motivation:
- Customers push long context (8k-64k tokens), pinned on Dedicated and Private. Our current serving runtime supports multiple attention implementations; runtime picks based on model config and sequence length heuristics.
- Recent customer reports: apparent latency regressions at 2k+ tokens for some models when running with bursty small-batch traffic and enabled KV cache. Hypothesis: interaction between prefix KV-cache reuse, paged attention memory recomputation, and degraded kernel scheduling.

What I profiled so far (high-level):
- Kernels: FlashAttention v2 (cuBLAS/soft-fused), our paged-attention path, fused-attention (single-kernel matmul+softmax+mm), and baseline naive attention (GEMM + custom softmax).
- Tools: Nsight Systems for end-to-end traces, Nsight Compute for per-kernel metrics, pprof for host stacks, cupy/cuda events for micro timings. Also used Triton microbench harness for kernel-level comparisons.
- Workloads: GPT-like decoder-only with 16-heads, head_dim=64, model widths tested: 1.5B and 13B analogs. Sequence lengths: 128, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8. KV-cache warm and cold scenarios.

Quick experimental commands (repro):
- Launch harness: python benchmarks/attn_harness.py --kernel flash --model 13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-warm --reps 200 --device 0
- Nsight capture: nsys profile --output=nsys_attn_flash_4k --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi python ...
- Nsight compute: ncu --target-processes all --set full --launch-skip 1 --launch-count 50 --import-source-only nsys_attn_flash_4k.qdrep

Findings (raw):
1) FlashAttention (v2)
- Fast for short to medium (<=2048) seqs for single-token generation: kernel throughput excellent, low SM utilization variance.
- For 4k+ seqs, observed increased L2 traffic and repeated device-to-host driver syncs from our runtime when swapping paged KV blocks. Nsight shows repeated small memcpy/host-sync events (~0.3-1ms each) in between attention calls when KV-cache eviction policy triggers.
- Tail latency: 95th/99th percentiles increase sharply when batch>1 under bursty arrival (interleaved requests). Hypothesis: flash kernels block on streaming of KV pages into GPU memory because they expect contiguous key/value tensors.

2) Paged attention path (our in-house paging)
- Designed to split KV into chunks and stream. Works well when streaming bandwidth saturated and kernel compute is the bottleneck.
- But when kernel compute is fast (FlashAttention), paging overhead dominates. Paging code introduces additional cudaMemcpyAsync calls plus host-thread coordination to manage page readiness — these appear in nsight as CPU stalls and driver work.
- Memory fragmentation: after multiple model loads/unloads (Dedicated heavy multiplexing test), we saw allocation retries that pushed latency to tens of ms. Need to add explicit allocator diagnostics.

3) Fused ops kernel (prototype fused softmax+matmul)
- Single-kernel fusion reduces device synchronization and eliminates materializing large intermediate softmax tensors.
- For long sequences with warm KV-cache (no paging), fused kernel beats FlashAttention by ~10-25% in end-to-end kernel time for 13B-equivalent config.
- However, code path currently not compatible with paged streaming; fusion assumes contiguous KV tensors. Extending fusion to streaming is non-trivial and would require tile-level accumulation and atomic adds or multi-pass reductions.

Micro metrics summary (example numbers, 13B, batch=1):
- seq=1024: Flash attention kernel time ~12.4 ms, fused ~10.9 ms, paged overall ~16.7 ms (paging overhead included).
- seq=4096: Flash ~74 ms, fused ~63 ms, paged ~95 ms (paging dominating).
- KV warm vs cold: cold (first access) adds ~6-12 ms due to page fetches depending on page size (2-16MB).

What I instrumented beyond kernel times:
- PCIe transfer sizes and frequency (from nsys) — critical to understand page size vs transfer overhead. We need to move to larger page granularity if the model architecture and latency SLOs allow.
- L2 cache hit/miss rates (ncu) — FlashAttention uses tiled shared memory patterns; as seq length grows, L2 misses rise and memory-bound behavior appears.
- SM occupancy and stall reasons — warp stalls primarily due to memory dependency for long seqs.

Open hypotheses / questions:
- Is our paging policy too eager? We currently prefetch next N pages where N=2. For some traces this causes unnecessary traffic; maybe adapt prefetch based on measured inter-request gap or request priority.
- Can we implement a low-latency path for single-request KV hits that bypasses page manager and pins contiguous KV when it fits?
- How much of the tail is caused by host-side coordination and not kernel execution? Nsight shows host threads blocking on a mutex in page manager during high concurrency. We should replace with lock-free ring/queues.

Short-term actionable items:
- Add telemetry gates in runtime to emit per-request page fetch count and total memcpy bytes. (owner: Hana)
- Implement a 1st-pass fused kernel compatible with tiled streaming (research approach: accumulate partial attention results per tile on-device and finalize with a small kernel). (owner: Ravi)
- Increase default page size for Dedicated GPUs in the config to 8MB for models >6B and measure impact. (owner: Leo)
- Add stress test that runs mixed seq-length workload with bursty arrivals to reproduce tail. (owner: Maya)

Longer-term ideas:
- Evaluate RDMA direct transfer (for Private on-prem) to reduce host-mediated page fetch costs.
- Work with FlashAttention upstream to expose a streaming-friendly API or hooks where we can feed non-contiguous KV as a list of segments (rather than contiguous buffer).
- Consider kernel-level page-aware attention: the kernel iterates pages internally and uses per-page shared memory staging to avoid host syncs. This is advanced but could pay off for 8k+ seqs.

Experiment logs (selected):
- 2025-02-20: baseline flash vs fused, seq 4096, batch1. nsys capture attached to PR 487. Observed fused 15% faster end-to-end.
- 2025-02-24: added nsight compute counters for L2 hit rate: for seq>=4096 L2 hit drops from 72% to 41% on A100.
- 2025-02-28: stress with batch=4, interarrival jitter 10-200ms — observed mutex contention in page manager; 95th increased by 3.6x.

Notes for reproducing locally (dev laptop/GPU):
- Make sure driver >= 525.x and CUDA 12.1 (some flash kernels expect sm_80). Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES accordingly.
- Use dataset with repeated short prefixes to simulate warm-KV and interleave cold requests to exercise paging.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Larger page sizes reduce frequency of host-device transfers but increase GPU memory pressure and may reduce batch parallelism. Need automated guardrails in scheduler: only allow large pages when free memory > threshold.
- Aggressive fusion reduces flexibility: harder to support multiple attention variants and fallback model-compatibility; need thorough validation.

Appendix / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add page-manager lock-free queue prototype (owner: Hana).
- [ ] Run dedicated 24hr stress with mixed TTL models to surface fragmentation (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Add per-request tracing id to correlate nsight traces with runtime logs (owner: Leo).
- [ ] Evaluate whether changing memory allocator (jemalloc vs default cuda malloc) affects fragmentation (owner: infra).

Questions for next sync:
- Can Product/Support share customer traces where latency tails started appearing? Need real traffic shape to prioritize.
- Is it OK to change default page size on Dedicated for new model images? Ops approval needed.

References / links (tickets & PRs):
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/487 (nsys captures + fused kernel prototype)
- Ticket: JIRA-INVEST-112 (attention kernel investigation)
- Internal note: confluence/Serving Runtime Kernel Notes v2

Final quick take:
- FlashAttention is great for contiguous KV workloads and short-medium sequences. Paging overhead and host-coordination are where we lose ground for long sequences. Fused kernels show promise but we need to design streaming-friendly fusion and reduce host-side blocking. Next week: prototyping lock-free page manager + run A/B with increased page size to quantify tradeoffs.
